Arthur Quiller-Couch, comp.  The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse.  1922.

Wood-Song

Eugene Lee-Hamilton (1845–1907)

W
HEN
 we are gone, love,
Gone as the breeze,
Woods will be sweet, love,
Even as these.
Sunflecks will dance, love,
Even as now,
Here on the moss, love,
Under the bough.
Others unborn, love,
Maybe will sit
Here in the wood, love,
Leafily lit;
Hearking as now, love,
Treble of birds;
Breathing as we, love,
Wondering words.
Others will sigh, love,
Even as we:
‘Only a day, love,’
Murmurs the bee.
